description: PyHeatDemand is a Python package for processing heat-demand inputs at building, street, district or larger geographic scales. The JOSS paper and own README describe raster, polygon, point and address inputs and harmonization to a target grid. A user chooses the study area, data sources, grid size and year; the package does not publish a global heat-demand surface. The own repository reports GPL-3.0. Its outputs can inform district-heating network planning, geothermal siting and heat-supply capacity simulations. The tool can also derive demand estimates from building and population features when direct values are unavailable. A caveat is that inferred heat demand depends on the quality and date of property records and on the chosen allocation rules. A harmonized map does not verify actual metered consumption. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own source were inspected without downloading heat-demand data or running the workflow.
name: PyHeatDemand heat-demand preparation
notes: G5 G5-0740. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
